He lost his factory job. So he built a submarine.
Wuhan, 2008. Zhang Wuyi gets laid off from a textile machine factory.
Instead of a new job, he starts on a submarine.
In a basement workshop, he welds an iron sub for two.
He says it dives thirty metres, and can stay down up to ten hours.
His first customer? A sea cucumber businessman from Dalian.
Who says he caught fifty kilos in forty minutes.
Soon Zhang has about ten workers.
One problem: subs with people inside don't pass the official checks.
So he takes the people out.
His remote control sub passes a lake test, and gets a patent.
In China, a layoff can be a launch. Find yours at laowai dot ma.
